readout_other: STN LFP spectral power and beta bursts via Percept PC; MDS-UPDRS-III; accelerometer finger-tapping velocity
direction_notes: M1 tbTUS reduced STN beta power and increased theta relative to sham and was associated with modest MDS-UPDRS-III improvement; GPi tbTUS increased beta without clinical improvement; occipital control had no significant effect.
safety_notes: Fatigue in nine sessions (19%) and brief scalp tingling, pain or heating in four sessions (9%); no neurological examination changes; simulated brain temperature rise below 0.19 C.

timing.protocol_description: Theta-burst TUS (tbTUS) lasting 120 s per hemisphere, delivered with neuronavigation to the M1; active sessions at least 1 week apart; LFP recorded during sonication and at 10, 30 and 45 min after.
Theta-burst TUS (tbTUS) lasting 120 s per hemisphere, delivered with neuronavigation to the GPi; active sessions at least 1 week apart; LFP recorded during sonication and at 10, 30 and 45 min after.

Theta-burst TUS (tbTUS) lasting 120 s per hemisphere, delivered with neuronavigation to the Occ (active control); active sessions at least 1 week apart; LFP recorded during sonication and at 10, 30 and 45 min after.

source_quotes.n_subjects: were investigated in 17 patients with PD
source_quotes.n_sessions_per_subject: Each patient underwent one active and one sham session in a randomized, single blinded order, and a subset (13 of 17) completed a third session, which was always active.
source_quotes.exposures[0].free_field.isppa_w_cm2: Free-field acoustic simulations using BabelBrain software at a spatial peak pulse average intensity (I<sub>SPPA</sub>) of 30 $\mathrm { W } / { \mathrm { c m } } ^ { 2 }$ were performed under water conditions for two focal depths—61 mm (representing the GPi) and 34 mm (representing cortical targets)—because 30 W/ $\mathrm { c m } ^ { 2 }$ is the maximum output available to end users on the NeuroFUS device.
source_quotes.exposures[0].in_situ.isppa_w_cm2: The Occ had the highest values for both I<sub>SPPA</sub> $( 5 \pm 1 . 6 \mathrm { W } /$ $\mathsf { c m } ^ { 2 } )$ and MI $( 0 . 4 8 \pm 0 . 0 8 ) $ , which were significantly higher than those observed in the M1 $( 3 . 2 \pm 1 . 4 \mathrm { W } / \mathrm { c m } ^ { 2 }$ and $0 . 3 8 \pm 0 . { \bar { 0 8 } }$ , respectively; $P _ { \mathrm { a d j } } < 0 . 0 0 1$ for both) and higher than those in the GPi for $I _ { \mathrm { S P P A } }$ only $( 4 . 4 \pm 1 . 2 \mathrm { W } / \mathrm { c m } ^ { 2 }$ and $0 . 4 5 \pm 0 . 0 7$ , respectively; $P _ { \mathrm { a d j } } < 0 . 0 5$ for $I _ { \mathrm { S P P A } }$ and $P _ { \mathrm { a d j } } = 0 . 1 3$ for MI).

flags.reason: Carrier frequency, pulse duration, PRF and duty cycle of the tbTUS protocol are not stated in the main text (Fig. 1B legend only defines TBD, PRI, SD abbreviations).
120 s per hemisphere comes from the Fig. 1 legend, not the Methods.

30 W/cm2 is the simulated free-water Isppa used for planning (maximum output of the device), not a measurement; in situ values are per-target BabelBrain simulation means across 20 hemispheres of 10 patients.
Every patient had one sham and one active session; 13 of 17 had a third active session; recorded as [2,3].
Occipital target given as middle occipital gyrus in the Discussion; recorded as occipital lobe.
M1 tbTUS reduced STN beta and raised theta, GPi tbTUS increased beta; direction depends on target.
